scope: Static recertification of the passive readers for the game's update of 15 October 2026 (Nexus LastGameBuild 208704). File on disk only: no process was opened, read or probed. Not a live reading.

from.available: no: the file was replaced by the update; what is known of it is docs/audit/2026-10-13-recertification-build-208574.json (RVAs, digests, vtables) and the wallet guard bytes kept in core/tests/fixtures/wallet_profile.json

method: Layout: the PE header of the new file was compared with the one recorded for the build of 13 October 2026. Image base, image size and every section's RVA, virtual size and file offset are the same.

Ranges: each of the 37 ranges the three profiles keep by digest was hashed at the RVA the recertification of 13 October gave it. The method of that day was also run in full: every offset of .text for ranges of 16 bytes or less, every 16-byte-aligned offset of .text for the others and every 8-byte-aligned offset of .rdata for the hash table were hashed and compared with the digests (aligned_search_hits; ranges that start off a 16-byte boundary are found only at their RVA). No range needed rebuilding: none has a byte that differs from the build of 13 October, so no rel32 field, image-relative displacement or jump table entry moved.
Vtables: the slots the readers check were read at the RVAs of 13 October and hold the proven functions; the rip-relative lea instructions of .text that refer to each vtable were counted.
Functions the inventory reader compares by address only were disassembled in the new file and compared with the route of inventory_reader_v3.py, as on 13 October.
The fixture profiles were carried to the new hash and checked with the audit's own check_profile_offline.py (unchanged) against a copy of the installed file.
tooling: Python 3.14 with capstone 5.0.7 in a scratch venv; the scripts read a copy of Gw2-64.exe in a scratch directory and are not retained

Item +0x58, the capacity at inventory +0xd0, definition +0x28 and the item context's +0x38 are not named by any range checked here and are assumed, as on 13 October.
